title: calypso-education-inference-efficiency-brainstorm-q2-2026
body:
Context and objective:

Quick working notes for the Calypso Education pilot (K12 adaptive tutoring). Goal: estimate before/after inference economics for their primary recommendation service and sketch an actionable rollout that preserves 95th-percentile latency SLO (<= 220ms per response) while cutting monthly token spend by >= 35%. Use this doc as the single place for assumptions before we move to a formal sheet.

Customer profile (summary):
- Calypso Education: adaptive Q&A and hints generator.
- Production workload: ~65M tokens/month (tokens counted after client-side pretokenization), 1.1M requests/month, avg response length 60 tokens, peak QPS 45 (US-east), 95th perc latency target 220ms.
- Current model: open-gpt-13b-finetuned (float16), single-variant serving, no prefix caching, minimal batching (client-side throttle).
- Current monthly bill (hosted): ~$32,400 (hosted token charges + request overheads). This is the number Calypso is paying today to their cloud provider through our hosted API.

Observed perf/trace highlights (from Calypso demo traces):
- Median latency: 180ms; 95th: 410ms (spikes during bursts).
- Long tail correlated with cold KV-cache misses and request bursts that bypass batching.
- Many requests have high overlap in prefixes (templated prompts by session type).

High-level optimization levers we can apply (ranked by expected impact):
1) Prefix/KV caching (autopopulate for templated prompts) — expected 20–30% token reduction for RL-based hints flows.
2) Moderate quantization (int8/4-bit with Redwood quant profiles) — 25–40% per-token cost cut with small quality risk on rare prompts; candidate for canary.
3) Aggressive continuous batching on steady-state traffic (server-side adaptive batching) — 10–18% CPU/GPU utilization improvement, improves tail latency when combined with smart routing.
4) Model variant routing (mix of 7b-int8 for short answers + 13b-fp16 for long/complex) — estimated blended unit cost down 22% while preserving quality.
5) Response truncation and heuristic post-filtering for scaffolded hint steps — 5–10% fewer tokens.

Baseline (calculated from customer telemetry):
- Monthly tokens: 65,000,000
- Cost per 1M tokens (current model): $0.50
- Total token cost: $32,500 (matches customer bill, rounding differences allowed)
- Other infra/requests overhead: $1,900
- Total monthly inference spend: $34,400

Conservative scenario (Apply caching + batching only):
- Assumptions: prefix caching catches 18% of tokens, batching yields 12% unit improvement on remaining tokens (throughput and lower per-token GPU overhead). No quantization.
- Effective tokens billed: 65M * (1 - 0.18) = 53.3M
- Effective unit cost reduction from batching: 12% -> new unit cost = $0.50 * 0.88 = $0.44
- Token cost = 53.3M / 1M * $0.44 = $23,452
- Infra overhead improvements: -$700 (fewer requests hitting control plane)
- Total monthly spend: ~$22,752
- Estimated savings vs baseline: ~33.8% (~$11,648/month)

Ambitious scenario (caching + quantization + routing + batching):
- Assumptions: caching 22%; quantization blended effect reduces unit cost by 35% on quantized traffic; route 60% of requests to quantized 7b-int8 variant, 40% remain on 13b-fp16 for high-complexity prompts; batching 15% improvement.
- Step compute (approx):
  - Base tokens after caching: 65M * (1 - 0.22) = 50.7M
  - Token split: quantized tokens = 50.7M * 0.60 = 30.42M; fp16 tokens = 20.28M
  - Unit costs: fp16 unit = $0.50 * (1 - 0.15 batching) = $0.425; int8 unit = $0.50 * (1 - 0.35 quant +  -0.15 batching) approx $0.2825 (apply quant first, then batching)
  - Token costs: int8 cost = 30.42 * $0.2825 = $8,594; fp16 cost = 20.28 * $0.425 = $8,619
  - Combined token cost ≈ $17,213
  - Infra/control-plane improvements and fewer retries: -$1,200
  - Total monthly spend ≈ $16,013
  - Savings vs baseline ≈ 53.5% (~$18,387/month)

Quality/regression risk notes:
- Quantization: early A/B (10% traffic) against 13b-fp16 baseline for 2 weeks with automated evals on 8 critical prompt sets (pass threshold: avg ROUGE/ROUGE-L drop < 2% and zero regressions on safety checks).
- Routing logic: add fallback rule if model_variant_response_confidence < threshold OR latency > 300ms.
- Caching correctness: implement token-level TTLs and user-scoped keys (avoid mixing user-specific context).

Operational plan (canary -> scale):
1) Week 0-1: Instrument telemetry (per-variant token counts, 95th latency, cache hit rate) and add eval harness links (see linked artifacts).
2) Week 2: Deploy prefix/KV caching rules for templated prompts only (+ feature flag). Monitor cache hit and downstream latency.
3) Week 3-4: Enable server-side adaptive batching with conservative thresholds; test under synthetic burst load.
4) Week 5-6: Canary quantized 7b-int8 for 10% traffic with payload sampling for evals and human review of randomness-sensitive cases.
5) Week 7-8: Gradually increase quantized traffic to 60% while routing edge cases to 13b-fp16, validate metrics.

Estimated engineering tasks and owners (rough):
- Cache rule authoring + templates: Sofia Martinez (product) + Arjun Patel (eng) — 3 days
- Batcher tuning and metric hooks: Liam O'Connor (serving-runtime) — 1 sprint (5 working days + validation)
- Quantized runtime validation + canary infra: Rina Gupta (applied-ml) + runtime team — 2 sprints
- Eval harness (automated quality checks): Maya Chen (product) + applied-ml — 1 sprint

Simple risk-adjusted financial model (conservative weighting):
- P(Full success) = 0.45 -> savings 50%
- P(Partial success) = 0.35 -> savings 30%
- P(Margin case) = 0.20 -> savings 15%
- Expected weighted savings = 0.45*50% + 0.35*30% + 0.2*15% = 36.25%
- Expected monthly savings ≈ $12,470 (on baseline $34,400)

Open questions for the customer/next steps:
- Can Calypso provide a prioritized list of 10 canonical prompt templates (we need these to seed cache rules)?
- Any SLA tolerance for brief (1–3 day) degradation during canary?
- Will Calypso accept a 7b-int8 variant serving for short/hint responses?

Deliverables to produce next:
- Formal spreadsheet with scenario sensitivity (tokens, unit costs, hit-rate sweeps) — Evelyn will draft (sheet template attached in linked artifacts).
- Canary playbook: step-by-step rollback and escalation playbook (owner: Liam).
- Eval automation job (owner: Maya / Rina).

Notes to self (informal brainstorm fragments):
- Might try aggressive token compression for metadata-heavy responses (strip JSON keys on server-side).
- Explore prefix canonicalization for session scaffolds — could bump cacheable fraction by +8% if done right.
- Put hold point before quantization rollout: add human spot-check for edge-case cohorts (low-resource languages).

Bottom line (quick TL;DR to share with Calypso):
- Low-effort wins (caching + batching) can deliver ~30–35% reduction in monthly spend with minor risk to latency/quality.
- Combined approach including quantization and routing can realistically exceed 50% savings but requires a staged canary and close quality monitoring.
- Proposed next step: sync with Calypso engineering to get canonical prompts and calendar 2-week canary starting early April.

-- end of notes --
